substitutes: No muffin tin? Use a few paper cups or a cardboard tube with the ends folded.
title: The Doggy Dinner Reservation
clue: A table is booked for two, and one of you has strong opinions about the starter.
reveal: Turn tonight's regular dinner into an evening out. Write a reservation, greet your guest at the door and serve the usual meal in three courses, each in a different feeding style, while you enjoy your own dinner nearby.
objective: Serve your dog's regular dinner as a three-course restaurant evening with different feeding styles.
instructions: Measure tonight's dinner as usual and divide it into three small piles: starter, main and dessert. Nothing extra is added, so there is nothing new to think about.
Write a reservation card and a one-page menu with silly dish names for each course (Kibble Carpaccio, Pot Roast of the Day). Set a mat or towel as their table, away from your own food.
Greet them at the door like a host and show them to their table. Serve the starter scattered on a towel or snuffle mat so they can forage.
Bring the main in a muffin tin, a cardboard tube or a bowl, whichever your dog already handles well, and let them work at it. Pick up anything left when they walk away.

Serve dessert as the last few pieces on a clean plate or lick mat. Then clear the table and, for your own meal, keep it out of reach: onions, garlic, grapes, chocolate and anything sweetened with xylitol are unsafe.
Present the bill: a note of 'tip: one scratch behind the ears' and write down the dish they went back to first.
twist: The three courses are just the one regular dinner split three ways and served in different feeding styles, so it feels like a night out without adding a bite.
variations: Bowl-only: serve all three courses in the same bowl as separate small rounds.
No-food version: courses of play: a sniff of a scented cloth, a quiet toy and a cuddle.
For puppies: smaller piles and a flat plate. For seniors: a flat plate or mat at a comfortable height (ask your vet), and skip the tin.
For dogs on prescription or allergy diets: use only their prescribed food, split exactly as your vet advises.
completion: Your dog has been served all three courses, or as many as they wanted, and the table is cleared.
photoIdea: Your dog at their mat with the menu card beside them.
memoryPrompt: Which course did your dog visit first, and what is the house special?
dietNotes: Use only their regular dinner, split three ways, so the day's allowance is unchanged. Skip foraging styles if they guard food. Ask your vet about diet; prescription diets stay exactly as advised.
safety: Take everything from tonight's allowance and offer nothing toxic: never chocolate, grapes, raisins, onion, garlic or xylitol.
Supervise foraging toys and remove any that your dog chews apart or swallows.
Keep your own plate, drinks and candles away from them: no open flames, and no sharing.
teaser: Your dog has a reservation tonight, and the service is excellent.
